NDT (Hundman et al. 2018) vs existing pooled-percentile baseline, Own-Registry LOO, all 8 checkpoints, CPU/MEM/NET. NDT threshold computed from pooled calibration scores only (same calibration data existing baseline uses); test scoring reuses saved arrays from threshold_plot_evidence_full.json.

NDT v2 (Hundman et al. 2018) vs existing pooled-percentile baseline, Own-Registry LOO, all 8 checkpoints, CPU/MEM/NET. Fix vs v1: NDT z/eps computed separately per training topology (one coherent calibration stream at a time, same cu_fn_pool normalization as existing/test scores), then averaged into one applied threshold -- v1 pooled all training topologies into one array before computing mu/sigma, which inflated sigma and pushed z to the sweep's upper bound (10.0) every time, collapsing NET F1. Test scoring reuses saved arrays from threshold_plot_evidence_full.json.

NDT v3 (Hundman et al. 2018) vs existing pooled-percentile baseline, Own-Registry LOO, all 8 checkpoints, CPU/MEM/NET. v1->v2: NDT z/eps computed separately per training topology (one coherent calibration stream at a time, same cu_fn_pool normalization as existing/test scores), then averaged into one applied threshold -- v1 pooled all training topologies into one array before computing mu/sigma, which inflated sigma and pushed z to the sweep's upper bound (10.0) every time, collapsing NET F1 (v2 still mostly hit the z=10 boundary though, NET still collapsed). v2->v3: added EWMA smoothing (alpha=0.05) of both calibration and test score streams before NDT selection/thresholding, per Hundman Sec 3.1 (method assumes smoothed errors, not raw per-timestep scores). Test scoring reuses saved arrays from threshold_plot_evidence_full.json.

NDT (Hundman et al. 2018, per-topology eps averaged + EWMA-smoothed, reused from ndt_own_registry_results.json) vs existing pooled-percentile baseline, cross-registry both directions: small->big (4 original checkpoints -> cu0_7du/cu0_10du, reused saved full score arrays) and big->small (4 new checkpoints -> cu0_du0du1/cu2_du3du4du5, fresh model inference). CPU/MEM/NET.

DU-level NDT (Hundman et al. 2018) vs existing pooled-percentile (p99.5) baseline, 3-part scope (own-registry LOO, small->big, big->small), per-DU rows, own-file-only. NDT: per training-topology pooled-DU calibration stream, EWMA-smoothed, NDT-selected eps, averaged across the checkpoint's training topologies -- same recipe as CU NDT.

NEGATIVE RESULT: tested whether clamping the N_DU divisor (used only in slice_features for CU net_tx/net_rx normalization) to each checkpoint's own trained N_DU values (1-4), instead of the target's true out-of-range N_DU (7 or 10), could recover CU discriminative power on small->big targets without retraining. It does not -- clamping COLLAPSES already-good cases (e.g. cu0_du0du1->cu0_7du: 0.995-0.997 unclamped -> ~0.53 with any clamp value) and does not improve already-bad cases (cu0_10du stays ~0.53-0.55 regardless of clamp value 1/2/3/4, all identical). Root cause: raw CU traffic scales up with true N_DU, so dividing by the true (even out-of-range) N_DU brings values back toward the trained range; clamping to a smaller fixed divisor pushes the quotient further out of range instead, and all small clamp values collapse to the same degenerate floor -- confirms this is a genuine input-range/model-capacity limit, not a fixable-via-inference-time-hack issue. Conclusion: no cheap fix available; must either (a) use the already-validated wide-N_DU-spread checkpoints (cu1_du2/cu3_du6du7du8du9/cu0_7du/cu0_10du, trained across N_DU=1,4,7,10) for big targets, or (b) retrain the narrow checkpoints with a wider N_DU spread.
